questions.question: The large natural deposit of solid alkanes is known as which lake?
questions.explanation: The Pitch Lake is a large natural deposit of solid alkanes.

questions.question: Kolbe's method produces an alkane with which number of carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Kolbe electrolysis gives an alkane with an even number of carbon atoms.

questions.question: Normal alkanes from C5 to C17 are in which physical state?
questions.explanation: Alkanes with five to seventeen carbons are colourless liquids.

questions.question: Sulphonation of alkanes requires at least how many carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Alkanes with six or more carbon atoms undergo sulphonation.

questions.question: Lindlar catalyst reduces alkynes to which product?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen with Lindlar catalyst gives cis-alkenes.

questions.question: Terminal alkynes with ammoniacal copper(I) chloride give which precipitate?
questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes form a reddish copper(I) alkyne precipitate.

questions.question: Three moles of ethyne heated at 400 C with Ziegler catalyst gives which product?
questions.explanation: Ethyne trimerizes to benzene with Ziegler catalyst at 400 C.

questions.question: Thionyl chloride converts an alcohol into which product?
questions.explanation: Thionyl chloride replaces the hydroxyl group with chlorine.

questions.question: SN2 reaction consistently results in which stereochemical outcome?
questions.explanation: Backside attack in SN2 causes inversion of configuration.

questions.question: E1 elimination follows which rule for the major product?
questions.explanation: E1 elimination generally follows Zaitsev's rule to give the more substituted alkene.

questions.question: Protic solvents reduce the reactivity of which nucleophiles most?
questions.explanation: Protic solvents solvate small charged nucleophiles strongly through hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: Grignard reagents are formed from alkyl halides and which metal?
questions.explanation: Alkyl halides react with magnesium in ether to form Grignard reagents.

questions.question: The Wurtz reaction uses sodium metal in which solvent?
questions.explanation: Wurtz reaction occurs with sodium metal in dry ether.

questions.question: Buckminsterfullerene was named in honour of which professional?
questions.explanation: It honours Robert Buckminster Fuller, designer of geodesic domes.

questions.question: Which fullerene has been isolated and characterized as chiral?
questions.explanation: C76 is noted as a chiral fullerene.

questions.question: Doxil, a liposome-encapsulated drug, was approved in which year?
questions.explanation: Doxil was approved in 1995 to treat specific cancers.

questions.question: Graphene is roughly how many times stronger than steel?
questions.explanation: Graphene is about 200 times stronger than steel.

questions.question: Which instrument determines the surface charge of nanoparticles?
questions.explanation: Zeta potential analysis determines the surface charge of nanoparticles.

questions.question: Berzelius reduced K2SiF6 with molten potassium in which year?
questions.explanation: Berzelius reduced K2SiF6 with molten potassium in 1823.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid boils at which temperature?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid boils at 118 C due to strong hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: Butyric acid is found in which natural substance?
questions.explanation: Butyric acid is the common name for butanoic acid found in butter.

questions.question: A carboxylic acid with two COOH groups uses which suffix?
questions.explanation: Two carboxyl groups give the suffix -dioic acid.

questions.question: Grignard reagents react with carbon dioxide to give which product after protonation?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents add to CO2 to form carboxylic acids after protonation.

questions.question: Ammonolysis of an acid anhydride gives which product?
questions.explanation: Reaction of an acid anhydride with ammonia gives an amide.

questions.question: Which carboxylic acid derivative is the least reactive?
questions.explanation: Amides are the least reactive of the common carboxylic acid derivatives.

questions.question: Spodumene has which formula?
questions.explanation: Spodumene is LiAlSi2O6, the most abundant lithium mineral.

questions.question: Down's process keeps sodium chloride molten at which temperature?
questions.explanation: The NaCl is kept molten at 600 C using a eutectic mixture with CaCl2.

questions.question: Rubidium and caesium were discovered by which scientist?
questions.explanation: Robert Bunsen discovered rubidium and caesium in 1861.

questions.question: The caesium clock is used for which standard measurement?
questions.explanation: The caesium atomic clock defines the second and the metre.

questions.question: Lithium is the only alkali metal that forms which nitride?
questions.explanation: Lithium reacts with nitrogen to form lithium nitride, Li3N.

questions.question: Sodium reacts with oxygen to give which product?
questions.explanation: Sodium forms the peroxide Na2O2 with oxygen.

questions.question: Sodium carbonate is prepared by which industrial process?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate is prepared by the Solvay process.

questions.question: Lemery in 1675 divided compounds into how many sources?
questions.explanation: Lemery divided compounds into vegetables, mineral, and animal sources.

questions.question: Carl Wilhelm Scheele discovered tartaric and which other acid?
questions.explanation: Scheele discovered tartaric and citric acids.

questions.question: Berthelot is credited with synthesizing which compound?
questions.explanation: Berthelot synthesized methane from its elements.

questions.question: Organic compounds are carbon compounds except which of the following?
questions.explanation: Organic compounds exclude oxides, sulphides, hydrogen cyanide, carbonates, and bicarbonates.

questions.question: Antoine Lavoisier is considered the father of which field?
questions.explanation: Lavoisier is considered the father of modern chemistry.

questions.question: A plot of ln k versus 1/T gives a straight line with slope equal to which quantity?
questions.explanation: The slope of ln k versus 1/T equals -Ea/R.

questions.question: In the Arrhenius equation, A represents which term?
questions.explanation: A is the frequency factor in the Arrhenius equation.

questions.question: The first step in heterogeneous catalysis is which?
questions.explanation: The first step in heterogeneous catalysis is adsorption and activation of the reactants.

questions.question: The substance whose reaction an enzyme catalyzes is called which?
questions.explanation: The substance whose reaction the enzyme catalyzes is called the substrate.

questions.question: An unstable grouping of atoms that can break up to form products is called which?
questions.explanation: An activated complex is an unstable grouping of atoms that can break up to form products.

questions.question: Thortveitite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Thortveitite is the rare mineral of Scandium with formula (Sc,Y)2Si2O7.

questions.question: Vanadinite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Vanadinite is Pb5(VO4)3Cl, an ore of Vanadium and Lead.

questions.question: Pyrolusite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Pyrolusite is MnO2, the main ore of Manganese.

questions.question: Pentlandite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Pentlandite is (Ni, Fe)9S8, an ore of Nickel and Iron.

questions.question: Cuprite has which formula?
questions.explanation: Cuprite is Copper Oxide (Cu2O).

questions.question: Chromium has which anomalous electronic configuration?
questions.explanation: Chromium adopts [Ar] 3d5 4s1 due to the stability of a half-filled d sub-shell.

questions.question: EDTA is a classic example of which ligand type?
questions.explanation: EDTA binds through six donor atoms and is hexadentate.

questions.question: Cobalt blue pigment has which formula?
questions.explanation: Cobalt blue pigment is CoAl2O4.
